title: Overlapping Quorums Still Need Conflict Rules
description: A leaderless store uses N=3, R=2 and W=2. Two clients concurrently update one key. A teammate says overlapping quorums alone make the operation linearizable. What is missing?

options.text: A larger cache so the read can avoid the quorum.
options.explanation: Caching does not establish a single order for concurrent writes and can introduce another stale copy.

options.text: A rule for concurrent versions and the store's actual consistency protocol.
options.explanation: R+W>N guarantees set overlap under the stated replica assumptions, not a total order. Concurrent writes and sloppy quorums require additional reasoning.

options.text: Wall-clock timestamps, which always reveal the true last write.
options.explanation: Clocks drift and can jump. Last-writer-wins can discard data and does not turn overlap into consensus.

options.text: Changing to R=1 and W=1 to remove conflicting responses.
options.explanation: That removes even the overlap guarantee and can return stale values.
